originalTitle: Seventy years after South Africa’s women’s march, the struggle is not over
title: Super Women of South Africa: Heroes Then and Now!
content:
Hi everyone! It's your Africa Kids News reporter, ready to tell you an amazing story from South Africa! Get ready to learn about some very brave women who made a big difference, a long, long time ago, and how their bravery still helps us today!

A Long, Long Time Ago: The Brave Women's March!

Imagine a very, very long time ago. So long that it was 70 years ago! That's even before your grandma or grandpa was born! In South Africa, there used to be some rules that were not fair at all. These unfair rules were called 'apartheid'. It meant that people were treated differently just because of the color of their skin. It made people live 'apart' from each other, and it was not kind. One of these unfair rules was called a 'pass law'. This law made it very hard for Black people to move around their own country. They had to carry a special little book, almost like a passport, every single time they left their homes. If they didn't have this book with them, they could get into big trouble with the police. It was a very unfair rule that took away their freedom to go to school, work, or visit friends. Guess what? The government wanted to make these pass laws even stronger, and they wanted women to carry these books too! But the women of South Africa said, 'NO WAY! This is not fair!' They decided they had to do something big and brave to show how they felt.

A Big Walk to Say "NO!"

So, what did these incredible women do? They decided to walk! Not just a short walk, but a very, very big march! On a special day, 70 years ago, thousands and thousands of women came together. They came from all over South Africa – from small towns and big cities. They were Black women, White women, Indian women, and Coloured women. They all stood together, shoulder to shoulder, showing that they were strong and united. Can you guess how many women walked? There were about 20,000 women! That's like putting all the kids from many, many schools together! They walked to a very important building called the Union Buildings in a big city called Pretoria. This is where the country's government leaders work. They marched very quietly and bravely. They carried messages and signs that said, 'Women are not weak! We want freedom! We don't want pass laws!' They left lots and lots of petitions – which are like very important letters – at the doors of the government leader, saying 'Please, stop these unfair laws!' They also sang a very famous and powerful song that meant, 'You strike a woman, you strike a rock!' It showed how strong and determined they were. Did you know? The Union Buildings in Pretoria are still a very important place today, where the President of South Africa works!

A Big Win!

The brave march of these women made a huge difference. Their loud and clear message helped to show everyone that the pass laws were wrong. Because so many people, especially these brave women, kept fighting and saying 'NO!', eventually, those unfair pass laws were taken away! Hooray! This was a very big victory for freedom and fairness in South Africa. It showed everyone that when many people come together and speak up for what is right, they can change things for the better. The women of South Africa showed incredible courage and strength. They taught us that even when things are very hard, we must never give up fighting for what is fair and kind.

What's Happening Today?

Now, here’s the interesting part! Even though those pass laws are gone, and South Africa is a free country for everyone, the super spirit of those brave women is still needed today. Why? Because many girls and women in South Africa still face some difficult challenges. Sometimes, women face 'violence'. This means that some people are not kind or safe to women, and that is very, very wrong. Everyone, especially girls and women, deserves to feel safe and happy in their homes, at school, and everywhere they go. No one should ever hurt another person. Another challenge is 'poverty'. This means that some women and their families don't have enough money for important things like yummy food, warm clothes, or a nice, safe home. They work hard, but sometimes it's still not enough. Everyone deserves to have enough to live comfortably and happily. And some women face 'unemployment'. This means they want to work and have a job to earn money for their families, but they can't find one. It can be very hard when you want to work but there are no jobs available. Girls and women deserve good chances to learn and work, so they can follow their dreams. Did you know? Giving everyone a chance to go to school and have a job is called 'equality', and it makes a country stronger and happier!

Why We Still Need Heroes!

So, even though the big march was a long, long time ago, the struggle for women to be completely free, safe, and happy is still going on. The brave women of 70 years ago showed us how to stand up for what's right. And today, we still need to keep working hard so that all girls and women in South Africa can live wonderful lives. This means making sure that girls can go to school and learn, that women are safe from harm, and that they can find good jobs. It means treating everyone with kindness and respect, no matter if they are a boy or a girl, a man or a woman.

Let's All Be Super Helpers!

So, what can we, as kids, do? We can learn from these super women! We can always be kind to our friends, our sisters, and our mothers. We can make sure everyone feels safe and important. We can share our toys and be fair when we play. And we can remember that every girl and woman has big dreams, and they deserve to have all the chances to make those dreams come true. Let's all be super helpers and make South Africa an even better place for everyone, just like those brave women started doing 70 years ago! Thank you for listening to this important story! Bye-bye for now!
